reason: Both cover the same core flaws (self-selection, survivorship bias, voluntary-to-mandatory extrapolation, multiple comparisons, region-as-proxy, uncontrolled pre/post claim, percentage-point conflation), but A additionally flags two genuine and distinct gaps—no uncertainty/CI reported for the 31% retention figure and no effect size reported for the region finding—that materially affect whether the conclusions are warranted. B's extra 'reverse-causality' item largely restates the self-selection confound already covered elsewhere, adding redundancy rather than new substance.
